title: Pita Breakfast Pizza with Za'atar
shortDescription: Crisped pita, fried egg, feta, za'atar, olive oil
note: Broil the bare pita for a minute first so it stays crisp under the toppings instead of going soft.
introCopy: A whole breakfast on one round of bread — eggs, salty cheese, and the herby crunch of za'atar, ready before the coffee finishes brewing.

steps.text: Heat the broiler. Brush both sides of the pitas with half the olive oil and broil 1-2 minutes per side until lightly crisp.
Scatter spinach, tomatoes, and feta over the warm pitas.
In a nonstick pan, fry the eggs in the remaining olive oil to your liking.
Slide an egg onto each pita, sprinkle with za'atar and salt, and serve right away.

title: Feta and Spinach Frittata
shortDescription: Baked eggs, wilted spinach, feta, dill
note: Let the frittata sit for five minutes after baking — it firms up and slices much more cleanly.
introCopy: One pan, one oven pass, and a whole tray of breakfast that reheats just as well the next morning.

steps.text: Heat oven to 375°F. Warm olive oil in an oven-safe skillet and cook onion until soft, about 4 minutes.
Add spinach and cook, stirring, until wilted, about 2 minutes.
Whisk eggs with milk, salt, and pepper. Pour over the spinach and onion, then scatter feta and dill on top.
Transfer to the oven and bake until the center is just set, 15-18 minutes.
Rest 5 minutes, then slice into wedges.

title: 15-Minute Mediterranean Breakfast Bowls
shortDescription: Yogurt, cucumber, tomato, olives, egg, hummus
note: Use thick, unsweetened yogurt — it's standing in for both a dip and a dressing here.
introCopy: A savory bowl built from whatever's in the fridge door: yogurt, a soft egg, crunchy vegetables, and a smear of hummus to tie it together.

steps.text: Bring a small pot of water to a boil and soft-boil the eggs, 6-7 minutes. Cool under cold water and peel.
Divide yogurt between two bowls and spread into a shallow layer.
Arrange cucumber, tomatoes, olives, and a dollop of hummus over the yogurt.
Halve the eggs and nestle them on top. Drizzle with olive oil and serve.

title: Beet-Ginger Smoothie Bowl
shortDescription: Roasted beet, banana, ginger, frozen berries
note: A pre-cooked beet (vacuum-packed or leftover roasted) is what makes this fast — don't start from raw.
introCopy: Earthy beet and a warm hit of ginger turn a fruit smoothie into something that actually tastes like breakfast, not dessert.

steps.text: Blend the beet, banana, berries, ginger, and almond milk until smooth and thick.
Pour into bowls and top with granola or any extra fruit you like.

title: Banana-Chocolate Chia Pudding Parfait
shortDescription: Overnight cocoa chia pudding, banana, yogurt layers
note: Stir the chia mixture again after 10 minutes so it doesn't clump at the bottom of the jar.
introCopy: Set it before bed and breakfast is basically dessert by morning — thick cocoa pudding layered with banana and yogurt.

steps.text: Whisk chia seeds, milk, cocoa powder, and honey together. Let sit 10 minutes, then stir again to break up clumps.
Cover and refrigerate at least 4 hours, or overnight, until thickened to a pudding consistency.
Layer the chia pudding with banana slices and yogurt in glasses to serve.

title: Green Smoothie Bowl
shortDescription: Spinach, avocado, pineapple, banana, spirulina
note: Freeze the banana ahead of time — it's the difference between a drink and a spoonable bowl.
introCopy: Avocado gives this a creaminess most smoothies don't have, while pineapple keeps it from ever tasting like a salad.

steps.text: Blend spinach, avocado, pineapple, banana, coconut water, and spirulina until completely smooth.
Pour into bowls and top with fruit, seeds, or coconut flakes as you like.

title: Homemade Instant Oatmeal
shortDescription: Pre-mixed oats, cinnamon, flax, dried fruit
note: Make a big batch of the dry mix and portion it into jars — from there it really is just add hot water.
introCopy: The packet stuff without the sugar bomb: rolled oats blended fine with cinnamon and flax, ready in the time it takes the kettle to boil.

steps.text: Pulse 1 cup of the oats in a blender or food processor until finely ground; mix back with the remaining whole oats.
Stir in flaxseed, cinnamon, dried fruit, and salt. Store in a jar for future breakfasts.
For one serving, stir 1/2 cup of the mix with 1 cup boiling water or milk and let sit 2 minutes to thicken.

title: Mango Rose Smoothie Bowl
shortDescription: Mango, yogurt, rosewater, pistachio, cardamom
note: Go easy on the rosewater — a little smells like a garden, a lot smells like soap.
introCopy: Inspired by Middle Eastern mango-rose desserts but built for breakfast, with yogurt keeping it from tipping into dessert territory.

steps.text: Blend mango, yogurt, rosewater, cardamom, and enough milk to move the blades, until thick and smooth.
Pour into bowls and top with chopped pistachios.

title: Sweet Potato Hash Brown Waffle
shortDescription: Grated sweet potato pressed and crisped in a waffle iron
note: Squeeze the grated sweet potato dry in a towel first — excess moisture is what keeps it from crisping.
introCopy: The waffle iron does what a skillet can't: crisp edges all the way through, with no flipping and no soggy middle.

steps.text: Squeeze grated sweet potato in a clean towel to remove as much liquid as possible.
Mix with egg, cornstarch, 1 tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Heat a waffle iron, brush with remaining oil, and press in a thin, even layer of the mixture.
Cook until deeply golden and crisp, 6-8 minutes per batch. Repeat with remaining mixture.

title: Cucumber Radish Salad
shortDescription: Cucumber, radish, dill, lemon, olive oil
note: Salt the cucumber and radish for 10 minutes and drain before dressing — it keeps the salad crisp instead of watery.
introCopy: A cold, crunchy, five-minute salad that works as a side to almost anything grilled.

steps.text: Toss cucumber and radish slices with a pinch of salt and let sit in a colander 10 minutes, then drain.
Whisk olive oil, lemon juice, salt, and pepper together.
Toss the vegetables with the dressing and dill just before serving.

title: Caprese Salad
shortDescription: Tomato, fresh mozzarella, basil, olive oil, balsamic
note: Slice the tomatoes and mozzarella to the same thickness so each bite gets both.
introCopy: Three ingredients at their best need almost nothing done to them — just good tomatoes, fresh mozzarella, and basil.

steps.text: Arrange alternating slices of tomato and mozzarella on a platter, tucking basil leaves between them.
Drizzle with olive oil and balsamic glaze, then finish with flaky salt and pepper.

title: Shrimp Avocado and Feta Wrap
shortDescription: Seared shrimp, avocado, feta, greens, lemon in a wrap
note: Warm the tortilla briefly before rolling — it folds without cracking and holds together much better.
introCopy: A five-minute sear on the shrimp is the only cooking involved; everything else is assembly.

steps.text: Season shrimp with salt and pepper and sear in olive oil over medium-high heat until pink and opaque, about 4-5 minutes.
Warm the tortillas briefly in a dry pan or microwave.
Layer greens, avocado, shrimp, and feta down the center of each tortilla. Squeeze lemon juice over the top.
Fold in the sides and roll tightly. Slice in half to serve.

title: Yogi Lentil Bowl
shortDescription: Spiced lentils, rice, greens, turmeric-tahini dressing
note: Rinse lentils until the water runs clear so the finished dish isn't cloudy or gritty.
introCopy: A grounding, one-bowl lunch built around warm-spiced lentils and a bright turmeric-tahini dressing.

steps.text: Cook rice according to package directions.
Simmer lentils with cumin and half the turmeric in salted water until tender, 18-20 minutes, then drain.
Whisk tahini, lemon juice, remaining turmeric, olive oil, and a splash of water into a pourable dressing.
Build bowls with rice, lentils, and raw spinach, then drizzle with the dressing.

title: Grilled Romaine Salad with Avocado-Lime Dressing
shortDescription: Charred romaine, creamy avocado-lime dressing, cotija
note: Grill the romaine cut-side down and leave it — moving it too soon tears the leaves instead of charring them.
introCopy: A quick char turns romaine from a salad base into something worth grilling on purpose.

steps.text: Brush cut sides of the romaine with olive oil.
Grill cut-side down over medium-high heat until charred, about 2-3 minutes, without moving.
Blend avocado, lime juice, a splash of water, and salt into a thick dressing.
Drizzle grilled romaine with the dressing and scatter with cotija.

title: Brown Rice and Lentil Salad
shortDescription: Brown rice, lentils, herbs, lemon, olive oil
note: Dress the rice and lentils while still warm — they absorb far more flavor than once fully cooled.
introCopy: A make-ahead salad that only gets better after a night in the fridge, built to bulk up any lunch.

steps.text: Cook rice and lentils separately in salted water until tender, about 25-30 minutes each, then drain.
Combine warm rice and lentils in a large bowl with onion and parsley.
Toss with olive oil, lemon juice, salt, and pepper. Serve warm or chilled.

title: White Bean and Herb Zucchini Noodles
shortDescription: Spiralized zucchini, white beans, garlic, herbs, lemon
note: Salt the zucchini noodles and let them sit 10 minutes, then blot dry — otherwise the dish turns watery fast.
introCopy: A light, low-carb spin on pasta and beans, tossed together raw-warm rather than simmered into a stew.

steps.text: Salt the zucchini noodles, let sit 10 minutes, then blot dry with a towel.
Warm olive oil in a large skillet and cook garlic until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add white beans and cook, stirring, until warmed through, about 3 minutes.
Add zucchini noodles and toss just until softened, 2-3 minutes. Off heat, stir in basil, lemon juice, and parmesan.

title: Greek-Style Chicken Orzo
shortDescription: Lemon chicken, orzo, tomatoes, feta, oregano
note: Finish cooking the orzo directly in the pan juices — it soaks up far more flavor than boiling it separately.
introCopy: One skillet carries this from raw chicken to a finished, saucy orzo dinner in well under an hour.

steps.text: Season chicken and sear in 1 tbsp olive oil over medium-high heat until browned, 6-7 minutes. Remove.
Add remaining oil, onion, and garlic to the pan and cook until softened, about 4 minutes.
Stir in tomatoes, orzo, broth, and oregano. Return chicken to the pan and bring to a simmer.
Cover and simmer, stirring occasionally, until orzo is tender and chicken is cooked through, 12-15 minutes.
Remove from heat and scatter feta over the top before serving.

title: Low-Carb Eggplant Pizza
shortDescription: Roasted eggplant rounds, marinara, mozzarella, basil
note: Salt the eggplant slices and press dry before roasting — it keeps the pizza rounds from turning soggy under the sauce.
introCopy: Eggplant rounds stand in for a crust here, roasted until they hold their shape under sauce and cheese.

steps.text: Heat oven to 425°F. Salt eggplant rounds and let sit 10 minutes, then pat dry.
Brush both sides with olive oil, arrange on a baking sheet, and roast 15 minutes, flipping halfway.
Top each round with marinara and mozzarella, then return to the oven until cheese melts, about 8 minutes.
Scatter with fresh basil before serving.

title: Pasta Primavera
shortDescription: Pasta tossed with spring vegetables, garlic, parmesan
note: Cut all the vegetables to a similar size so they finish cooking at the same time.
introCopy: A pantry-plus-crisper-drawer dinner — whatever vegetables are on hand get a quick sauté and tossed through hot pasta.

steps.text: Cook pasta in salted boiling water until al dente, reserving 1 cup pasta water before draining.
Meanwhile, warm olive oil in a large skillet and sauté zucchini and bell pepper until just tender, 5 minutes.
Add garlic, tomatoes, and peas and cook 2-3 minutes more.
Toss the drained pasta into the skillet with parmesan and a splash of pasta water until glossy and combined.

title: Italian Potato Salad
shortDescription: Warm potatoes, celery, red onion, herb vinaigrette
note: Dress the potatoes while still warm from boiling — they absorb the vinaigrette far better than once cooled.
introCopy: No mayonnaise here — just a sharp herb vinaigrette soaking into warm potatoes, closer to a French bistro salad than a picnic side.

steps.text: Boil potatoes in salted water until fork-tender, about 15 minutes, then drain.
Whisk olive oil, vinegar, mustard, salt, and pepper together.
Toss warm potatoes with celery, red onion, and the dressing.
Stir in parsley and serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Tomato Basil Soup
shortDescription: Roasted tomatoes, garlic, basil, cream
note: Roasting the tomatoes first, rather than just simmering them, is what gives the soup real depth.
introCopy: A slow roast concentrates the tomatoes before they ever hit the pot, so the soup tastes like far more effort than it took.

steps.text: Heat oven to 425°F. Toss tomatoes, onion, and garlic with olive oil and roast until caramelized, about 35 minutes.
Squeeze garlic from its skin and blend with the roasted vegetables and broth until smooth.
Warm the soup in a pot, stir in cream and basil, and season to taste.

title: Greek Fish with Tomatoes and Onions (Psari Plaki)
shortDescription: White fish baked in tomato, onion, and olive oil sauce
note: Bake the sauce alone for 15 minutes before adding the fish so it's already thickened and the fish doesn't overcook.
introCopy: A classic Greek taverna dish — firm white fish baked slowly in a garlicky tomato sauce until it falls apart with a fork.

steps.text: Heat oven to 375°F. Warm olive oil in an oven-safe pan and cook onion and garlic until softened, 5 minutes.
Add tomatoes, salt, and pepper, and simmer 10 minutes to thicken slightly.
Nestle fish fillets into the sauce, spooning some over the top.
Bake until fish flakes easily, 18-20 minutes. Scatter with parsley before serving.

title: Zucchini Parmesan
shortDescription: Baked breaded zucchini, marinara, mozzarella
note: Salt and drain the zucchini slices first, or the breading turns soggy under the sauce.
introCopy: A lighter riff on eggplant parm, baked rather than fried, with zucchini standing in for the usual eggplant.

steps.text: Heat oven to 400°F. Salt zucchini rounds, let sit 10 minutes, then pat dry.
Mix breadcrumbs with half the parmesan. Dip zucchini in egg, then coat in the breadcrumb mix.
Arrange on a baking sheet and bake 15 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden.
Layer zucchini in a baking dish with marinara and mozzarella, then bake until bubbly, 12-15 minutes.

title: Cioppino (Seafood Stew)
shortDescription: Mixed shellfish and fish in a tomato-wine broth
note: Add the seafood in stages by cooking time, firmest fish first, shellfish and shrimp last, so nothing overcooks.
introCopy: A San Francisco fisherman's stew, built from a garlicky tomato-wine broth and whatever seafood looks best.

steps.text: In a large pot, cook onion and garlic in olive oil until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add crushed tomatoes and wine, and simmer 10 minutes to reduce slightly.
Pour in stock and bring back to a simmer.
Add fish first and cook 4 minutes, then mussels and shrimp, cooking until mussels open and shrimp are pink, 5-6 minutes more.
Discard any unopened mussels, stir in parsley, and serve in bowls.

title: Spinach Ravioli with Artichoke and Olives
shortDescription: Cheese ravioli tossed with artichoke, olives, lemon butter
note: Pat the artichoke hearts dry before searing so they brown instead of steam.
introCopy: Store-bought ravioli gets a Mediterranean upgrade with a quick pan sauce of artichokes, olives, and lemon.

steps.text: Cook ravioli in salted boiling water according to package directions, then drain, reserving 1/2 cup pasta water.
Melt butter in a large skillet and sear artichoke hearts until lightly golden, 4 minutes.
Add olives, lemon zest, and lemon juice, and cook 1-2 minutes more.
Add ravioli and a splash of pasta water, tossing gently to coat. Finish with parmesan.

title: One-Pot Spinach Chicken Feta Pasta
shortDescription: Chicken, pasta, spinach, and feta cooked in a single pot
note: Simmer the pasta directly in the broth with the lid slightly ajar so it cooks evenly without scorching the bottom.
introCopy: Everything, including the pasta, cooks in one pot — fewer dishes, and the pasta comes out seasoned all the way through.

steps.text: Sear chicken in olive oil in a large pot until browned, about 5 minutes.
Add onion and garlic and cook until softened, 3-4 minutes.
Stir in pasta and broth, bring to a simmer, and cook uncovered, stirring occasionally, until pasta is tender, about 14 minutes.
Stir in spinach until wilted, then top with feta before serving.

title: Mushroom Tofu Stir-Fry
shortDescription: Crispy tofu, mushrooms, garlic, ginger, soy
note: Press the tofu for at least 15 minutes before cooking — that's what lets it crisp instead of steam in the pan.
introCopy: A fast weeknight stir-fry that leans on mushrooms for meaty texture and a good hard sear on the tofu for contrast.

steps.text: Press tofu for 15 minutes to remove excess water, then cube and toss with cornstarch.
Sear tofu in 2 tbsp oil over medium-high heat until golden on most sides, about 6 minutes. Remove.
Add remaining oil and cook mushrooms until browned, 4 minutes. Add garlic and ginger and cook 1 minute more.
Return tofu to the pan, add soy sauce and sesame oil, and toss to coat.

title: Butternut Squash and Mushroom-Olive Veggie Lasagna
shortDescription: Layered lasagna with roasted squash, mushrooms, olives, ricotta
note: Roast the squash and mushrooms until well browned before layering — raw-in-the-lasagna vegetables release too much water.
introCopy: A weekend-project lasagna that swaps meat for roasted squash and mushrooms, with olives adding a briny counterpoint.

steps.text: Heat oven to 425°F. Toss squash and mushrooms with 3 tbsp olive oil, spread on a sheet pan, and roast until browned, 25 minutes.
Cook lasagna noodles according to package directions and drain.
Stir olives into the roasted vegetables. Mix ricotta with a pinch of salt.
Layer noodles, marinara, ricotta, roasted vegetables, and mozzarella in a baking dish, repeating to fill.
Cover with foil and bake at 375°F for 25 minutes, then uncover and bake 10 minutes more until bubbly.

title: Roasted Salmon and Cauliflower Rice Bowl
shortDescription: Roasted salmon, cauliflower rice, avocado, tahini drizzle
note: Roast the salmon skin-side down and don't flip it — it stays moist and the skin crisps on its own.
introCopy: A low-carb bowl that leans on one sheet pan for the salmon and a quick sauté for the cauliflower rice.

steps.text: Heat oven to 425°F. Rub salmon with 1 tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper, and roast skin-side down until just cooked through, 12-14 minutes.
Meanwhile, sauté riced cauliflower in the remaining olive oil until tender, about 5 minutes.
Whisk tahini with lemon juice and a splash of water into a drizzle-able sauce.
Build bowls with cauliflower rice, salmon, and avocado, then finish with the tahini drizzle.

title: Kale-Hemp Pesto
shortDescription: Kale, hemp seeds, garlic, lemon, olive oil pesto
note: Blanch the kale for 30 seconds first if you want a milder, less bitter pesto.
introCopy: A nut-free pesto that leans on hemp seeds for richness, tossed with pasta or spread on almost anything.

steps.text: Cook pasta in salted boiling water until al dente, reserving 1/2 cup pasta water before draining.
Blend kale, hemp seeds, garlic, olive oil, lemon juice, and parmesan into a thick pesto, thinning with pasta water as needed.
Toss the pesto through the hot pasta until evenly coated.

title: Poached Cod
shortDescription: Cod gently poached in tomato, olive oil, and herb broth
note: Keep the poaching liquid at a bare simmer, never a boil — that's what keeps the cod tender instead of rubbery.
introCopy: A gentle, forgiving way to cook fish: cod simmered low in a light tomato broth until it just flakes apart.

steps.text: Warm olive oil in a wide pan and cook shallot until soft, 3 minutes.
Add tomatoes and broth, bring to a simmer, and cook 8 minutes to soften.
Lower to a bare simmer, nestle in the cod, cover, and poach until it flakes easily, 8-10 minutes.
Scatter with parsley and spoon the broth over each fillet to serve.

title: Honey Mustard Salmon with Root Vegetables
shortDescription: Sheet-pan salmon and roasted roots in a honey-mustard glaze
note: Give the root vegetables a head start in the oven — salmon cooks much faster and will finish long before they do.
introCopy: One sheet pan, one glaze, and dinner is basically hands-off once everything's in the oven.

steps.text: Heat oven to 400°F. Toss carrots and parsnips with 2 tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper, and roast 15 minutes.
Whisk honey, both mustards, and remaining olive oil together.
Push vegetables to the sides, add salmon to the pan, and brush everything with the honey mustard glaze.
Roast until salmon is just cooked through and vegetables are tender, 12-14 minutes more.

title: Grilled Vegan Pizza
shortDescription: Grilled pizza dough, marinara, grilled vegetables, vegan cheese
note: Grill the dough on one side first, then flip and top it on the grill — topping raw dough over direct heat makes it burn before the top cooks.
introCopy: The grill gives the crust a smoky char that the oven can't quite match, topped simply so it grills fast.

steps.text: Brush zucchini and bell pepper with 1 tbsp olive oil and grill until charred and tender, about 5 minutes; slice.
Stretch dough into rounds and brush both sides with remaining olive oil.
Grill dough on one side until grill marks form, 2-3 minutes, then flip.
Quickly top the grilled side with marinara, grilled vegetables, and vegan cheese. Close the lid until cheese melts, 3-4 minutes.

title: Stuffed Portobello Mushrooms
shortDescription: Portobello caps filled with spinach, breadcrumbs, feta
note: Scrape the gills out of the portobello caps with a spoon first — otherwise the filling pools in dark liquid as it bakes.
introCopy: Meaty mushroom caps stand in for a bun or a bowl, baked until tender with a savory, cheesy filling.

steps.text: Heat oven to 400°F. Brush mushroom caps with 1 tbsp olive oil and place gill-side up on a baking sheet.
Warm remaining oil in a pan, cook garlic 30 seconds, then wilt in spinach.
Off heat, stir in breadcrumbs and feta. Spoon the filling into the mushroom caps.
Bake until mushrooms are tender and the tops are golden, 18-20 minutes.

title: Mediterranean Tomato Feta Salad
shortDescription: Tomato, cucumber, red onion, feta, olives, oregano
note: Slice the block of feta rather than crumbling it — the classic version keeps it whole and lets each person break it apart.
introCopy: A simple village salad, closer to what's actually served across Greece than the chopped versions most people know.

steps.text: Arrange tomatoes, cucumber, and red onion on a platter.
Scatter olives over the top and lay the sliced feta over everything.
Drizzle with olive oil and sprinkle with oregano just before serving.

title: Turkish Gözleme (Spinach and Feta Stuffed Flatbread)
shortDescription: Hand-rolled flatbread folded around spinach and feta
note: Roll the dough as thin as you can manage — a thick gözleme steams instead of crisping in the pan.
introCopy: A street-food staple across Turkey: a simple dough rolled paper-thin, folded around a savory filling, and dry-fried until blistered.

steps.text: Knead flour, water, and salt into a smooth dough. Rest, covered, for 20 minutes.
Divide dough into 4 pieces and roll each out as thin as possible.
Scatter spinach and feta over half of each round, then fold into a rectangle to enclose the filling.
Dry-fry each gözleme in a hot skillet, brushing with butter, until blistered and golden on both sides, 3-4 minutes per side.

title: Tunisian Brik au Thon
shortDescription: Crisp phyllo parcels with tuna, potato, egg, and capers
note: Work fast once the egg is in — the parcel needs to be sealed and in the pan before the yolk sets, so it stays runny inside.
introCopy: A Tunisian classic: shatteringly crisp phyllo wrapped around a filling built to hide a soft, running egg yolk.

steps.text: Mix mashed potato, tuna, capers, and parsley together with salt and pepper.
Lay a phyllo sheet flat, spoon a quarter of the filling onto one half, and make a small well in the center.
Crack an egg into the well, then quickly fold the phyllo over into a half-moon and press the edges to seal.
Fry in hot oil until golden and crisp, about 2 minutes per side. Repeat with remaining parcels.

title: Roasted Broccoli with Lemon
shortDescription: High-heat roasted broccoli, garlic, lemon, parmesan
note: Give the broccoli space on the pan — crowding it steams the florets instead of letting the edges char.
introCopy: High heat is what turns broccoli from bland to genuinely craveable, with crisp, browned edges and a bright hit of lemon.

steps.text: Heat oven to 450°F. Toss broccoli with olive oil, garlic, salt, and pepper, and spread in a single layer on a sheet pan.
Roast until deeply browned at the edges, 15-18 minutes.
Toss with lemon zest, lemon juice, and parmesan while still hot.

title: Red Pepper Walnut Dip
shortDescription: Roasted red pepper, walnuts, garlic, pomegranate molasses
note: Toast the walnuts before blending — raw walnuts leave the dip tasting flat.
introCopy: Muhammara, a smoky-sweet Middle Eastern dip built from roasted peppers and walnuts, with pomegranate molasses for tang.

steps.text: Toast walnuts in a dry pan over medium heat until fragrant, about 4 minutes.
Blend peppers, walnuts, breadcrumbs, garlic, pomegranate molasses, olive oil, and cumin until mostly smooth with some texture.
Season with salt and let sit 15 minutes before serving to let flavors settle.

title: Balsamic Vinaigrette
shortDescription: Balsamic vinegar, dijon, olive oil, honey
note: Add the oil slowly while whisking to help it emulsify instead of separating right away.
introCopy: A five-minute pantry vinaigrette that upgrades almost any green salad without needing a trip to the store.

steps.text: Whisk balsamic vinegar, mustard, and honey together in a small bowl.
Slowly whisk in olive oil until emulsified. Season with salt and pepper.
Store in a sealed jar in the fridge for up to a week; shake before using.

title: Ayran (Turkish Salty Yogurt Drink)
shortDescription: Whisked yogurt, cold water, salt, mint
note: Chill the glasses along with the ayran — it's meant to be drunk ice-cold, not just cool.
introCopy: A savory yogurt drink that's the traditional companion to grilled meats across Turkey, closer to a lassi than a smoothie.

steps.text: Whisk yogurt, cold water, and salt together until smooth and frothy.
Pour over ice and garnish with mint.

title: Zaalouk (Moroccan Eggplant Salad)
shortDescription: Cooked-down eggplant and tomato with garlic and cumin
note: Let the eggplant break down fully into a soft, spreadable texture — it should look more like a chunky dip than a salad.
introCopy: A warm-spiced Moroccan eggplant salad, cooked low and slow until it's soft enough to scoop up with bread.

steps.text: Warm olive oil in a large pot and cook garlic until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add eggplant, tomatoes, cumin, and paprika, and stir to combine.
Cover and cook over low heat, stirring occasionally, until completely soft and jammy, 20-25 minutes.
Mash lightly with a fork, stir in cilantro, and season with salt to taste.
